case_name: Amar Singh Randhawa and Others v State of Punjab
respondent:
State of Punjab
Supreme Court of India

17 December 1976
Cr.A. No. 100 of 1973 (Cr.A. No. 51 of 1972, D/- 7 September 1972 (Punj & Har)), Dt. 17 December 1976.
The Judgment was delivered by : GUPTA, J.
1.  On March 20, 1971 three persons were murdered and three
facts: On March 20, 1971 three persons were murdered and three others injured in an incident in village Chalela in District Patiala.
The names of the persons murdered are Bakhtawar Singh, Amar Singh who was Sarpanch of the village, and Gurdev Singh.
Ten persons including the seven appellants before us were arrested in connection with the crime and tried by the Additional Sessions Judge, Patiala, and convicted as follows :
Amar Singh Randhawa was convicted u/s. 302 of the Indian Penal Code on three counts and was sentenced to death on each count.
Gurmit Singh accused was convicted u/s. 302 of the Indian Penal Code on two counts and was sentenced to death on each count.

Santa Singh and Nasib Singh were convicted u/s. 307 of the Indian Penal Code and were sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for five years each while the remaining eight accused were convicted under Section 307/149 of the Indian Penal Code and were sentenced to five years rigorous imprisonment.

Amar Singh Randhawa, Gurmit Singh and Gurdial Singh were convicted u/s. 307 and were sentenced to five years rigorous imprisonment each while the remaining seven accused were convicted under Section 307/149 of the Indian Penal Code and were sentenced to five years rigorous imprisonment.
All the accused were also convicted u/s. 148 of the Indian Penal Code and were sentenced to two years rigorous imprisonment each.
issues: The case against the accused was not true
The prosecution case is that Amar Singh, Sarpanch of village Chalela, had instituted proceedings for eviction of persons in unlawful possession of some land which vested in the panchayat.
What happened on March 20, 1971 appears from the evidence of the witnesses who had sustained injuries and the other eye-witnesses.
petitioner_arguments: The first circumstance to which counsel referred is the late delivery of the special report to the IInd Magistrate.
The F.I.R. was lodged at 5.30 p.m. on March 20. The said report was given at 6.15 p.m. to constable Lachhman Singh (P.W. 14) to be delivered to the Magistrate at Bassi.
respondent_arguments: The trial Court accepted the prosecution case in its entirety and convicted the ten accused persons as already stated.

The High Court acquitted three of the accused, namely, Dharampal Singh, Gurnam Singh and Rattan Singh on the ground that the case against them had not been proved beyond reasonable doubt and maintained the conviction of the rest while reducing sentence as mentioned above in the case of Amar Singh Randhawa and Gurmit Singh.
court_reasoning: The trial Court believed the explanation given by Lachhman Singh for the delay.

The High Court acquitted three of the accused, namely, Dharampal Singh, Gurnam Singh and Rattan Singh on the ground that the case against them had not been proved beyond reasonable doubt and maintained the conviction of the rest while reducing sentence as mentioned above in the case of Amar Singh Randhawa and Gurmit Singh.
holding: The seven accused whose conviction was affirmed by the High Court are the appellants before us.
The sentences were ordered to run concurrently.
